published_basis.source: Oliver Kullmann, Constraint Satisfaction Problems in Clausal Form I: Autarkies and Deficiency
published_basis.map: There is a polynomial-time reduction S(F) that is satisfiability-equivalent to F, does not increase maximal deficiency, and after which every assignment v=epsilon decreases maximal deficiency by at least one.
published_basis.formal: For every v in var(S(F)) and epsilon in {0,1}, delta*(<v=epsilon>*S(F)) <= delta*(S(F))-1.

exact_branch_semantics.descent: Both child branches strictly decrease delta* after the published preprocessing map.
exact_branch_semantics.problem: Keeping one arbitrary child is not satisfiability-equivalent; keeping both preserves exactness but creates an OR-branching state whose naive size is exponential in the rank.

frontier_shift.old_question: Find a polynomially computable strict rank.
frontier_shift.new_answer: A branchwise strict polynomially computable rank already exists: maximal deficiency after S(F).
frontier_shift.new_question: Can the exact OR of the two descended child obligations be merged into one polynomial-size, polynomial-update state while preserving exact SAT semantics for arbitrary 3CNF?
frontier_shift.name: EXACT_POLYNOMIAL_OR_MERGE

relation_to_prior_TRUMP_barriers: Davis-Putnam resolution is one exact CNF-level implementation of existential branch merge, but the pure resolution route has exponential lower-bound families (R43).
Full-function structured compilation is another exact merge/representation strategy, but structured DNNF routes have final/intermediate exponential state barriers (R44AC).
These barriers do not prove that every SAT-sufficient OR-merge representation is impossible.

next_admissible_math.target: One concrete exact OR-merge invariant M(A,B)
requirements: M represents SAT(A) OR SAT(B) exactly
M is computable in polynomial charged work
repeated merge preserves a polynomially bounded strict global rank
no hidden proof search, advice, exponential branch list, or full-function compilation debt
